name: Jinko Tiger Neo 430W
notes: Technology: N-Type TOPCon cells, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass, spanning four cell counts (108, 120, 132 and 144 half-cell) across an unusually wide 430-630W range. Pros: TOPCon's low degradation and good low-light performance at a competitive price; the 430-440W bins have the lowest Voc in the series, useful for longer strings. Cons: the 630W top bin's 132-cell layout pushes Isc to 16.2A - the highest current in this file - and needs a 30A series fuse against 25A for every other bin, so check MPPT current headroom carefully before selecting it.

name: Jinko Tiger Neo 3.0 460W
notes: Technology: N-Type TOPCon cells, 192 half-cell (48x4), monofacial with dual 2.0mm+2.0mm glass in the standard 1762x1134mm residential format. Runs 460-485W in 5W steps - JinkoSolar's newest generation, succeeding the original Tiger Neo line at the same footprint. Pros: efficiency rises to a class-leading 24.27% at the 485W top bin, and the glass-glass build adds durability over a single-glass panel without changing the footprint. Cons: monofacial only, so it forgoes the rear-side yield of the bifacial Tiger Neo 3.0 Bifacial counterpart at the same wattage.

name: Jinko Tiger Neo 3.0 Bifacial 460W
notes: Technology: N-Type TOPCon cells, 192 half-cell (48x4), genuinely bifacial with dual 2.0mm+2.0mm glass in the same 1762x1134mm residential format as the monofacial Tiger Neo 3.0 line. Runs 460-485W in 5W steps with an 85%+-5% bifaciality factor. Pros: real rear-side yield on a suitable mounting on top of the same class-leading 24.27% top-bin efficiency as the mono version, plus the same 15-year product / 30-year linear power warranty. Cons: bifacial gain depends on mounting height and ground reflectivity, so on a flush in-roof mount it offers little advantage over the cheaper monofacial version.
